contributor.persName: Hans Christian Andersen after Carlo Gozzi's "Il corvo"

history.p: Hartmann and Hans Christian Andersen were only twenty five years old - they were both born in 1805 - when they started working on "Ravnen". Hartmann was not Andersen's first choice, he had already asked Ivar Bredal and Friedrich Kuhlau, but both declined. The text is an adaptation of the Venetian nobleman and dramatist Carlo Gozzi's "Il corvo". The premiere and the following five performances were received very favourably by the audience, but the opera was nevertheless taken off the bill and only received one single performance a year later. In 1846 Hartmann and Andersen decided to revise the opera drastically, the spoken dialogue was substituted by recitatives and new characters added, but when is was staged twenty years later in April 1865 it was such a failure that Hartmann decided never to write an opera again.

Being written in purple ink in Hartmann's hand indicates that it is a much later addition.

titlePage.p: Ravnen. / Eventyr-opera i fire Acter. / Musiken af J.P.E. Hartmann. Opført første Gang i sin gamle Skikkelse, som Syngestykke i tre Acter med Dialog, paa det kongelige Theater den 29de October 1832. Med Dialogens Forandring til Recitativer, og paany gjennemarbejdet af Forfatter og Componist atter opført første Gang den 23de April 1865. / H.C. Andersens samlede Skrifter. XI 2. Udg.
